name: ACT New Zealand
slogan: Campaigns on smaller government, lower tax and individual choice.

details.overview: ACT is a right-wing political party that emphasises individual freedom, personal responsibility, equal legal rights, private enterprise, economic growth and a smaller, more efficient government. ACT argues that government should focus on essential services while giving individuals and businesses greater freedom to make their own decisions.
details.currentStatus: The party is led by David Seymour, who is also Deputy Prime Minister.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Reduce government spending, regulation and bureaucracy, promote private investment and productivity, and support lower taxes where financially sustainable. ACT argues that economic growth and higher productivity are the primary ways to improve incomes and living standards.

policyAreas.title: Government
policyAreas.text: Reduce the size and complexity of government, with fewer departments and clearer ministerial accountability. ACT argues that government should provide better services while costing taxpayers less.

policyAreas.title: Law & order
policyAreas.text: Support tougher consequences for serious and repeat offending, stronger protections for victims and measures targeting gangs and criminal behaviour. ACT supports the restoration of Three Strikes legislation and a more enforcement-focused approach to crime.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Focus government health spending on frontline services, improving access and reducing waiting times, while emphasising efficiency and measurable outcomes. ACT has also supported faster approval and funding of medicines.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Emphasise literacy, numeracy, school attendance, academic achievement and greater choice in education. ACT supports charter schools and stronger accountability for educational outcomes.

policyAreas.title: Housing & infrastructure
policyAreas.text: Reduce planning and regulatory barriers to building, strengthen property rights and encourage councils to enable more housing and infrastructure development.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Support employment, flexibility and economic growth while seeking to reduce what ACT considers unnecessary employment regulation and compliance costs for businesses.

policyAreas.title: Welfare
policyAreas.text: Place greater emphasis on moving people who can work from benefits into employment, with stronger obligations and time limits intended to reduce long-term welfare dependency.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & rural New Zealand
policyAreas.text: Reduce regulatory burdens on farmers, support primary-sector productivity and oppose environmental rules that ACT considers unnecessarily restrictive. ACT has supported reducing methane-reduction requirements and expanding access to oil and gas exploration.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Support environmental protection while placing greater emphasis on economic impacts, technological solutions and property rights. ACT has opposed what it considers overly costly climate regulations on agriculture and business.

policyAreas.title: Equal rights & Treaty policy
policyAreas.text: Emphasise equal legal rights for all New Zealand citizens regardless of ethnicity, gender or other characteristics. ACT opposes what it describes as race-based distinctions in government and has advocated redefining the legal interpretation of Treaty principles.

policyAreas.title: Immigration
policyAreas.text: Support immigration that fills genuine skills shortages and contributes economically, while proposing tighter requirements around skills, criminal offending, welfare eligibility and integration. ACT's current policy includes deportation provisions for certain serious offenders and a five-year stand-down from some benefits for residence-class migrants.

policyAreas.title: Firearms
policyAreas.text: Support firearm ownership for legitimate users while seeking stronger enforcement against criminal use and reforms to firearms regulation.

policyAreas.title: Business & regulation
policyAreas.text: Reduce red tape and regulatory requirements that ACT believes discourage investment, entrepreneurship and development. A major focus is expanding individual and property rights while limiting unnecessary government intervention.

details.position: ACT is generally positioned on the right, particularly on economic policy and the role of government. It places greater emphasis than National on individual freedom, private enterprise, personal responsibility, property rights and reducing government intervention. On some social issues, ACT also takes a strongly libertarian position, emphasising freedom of speech and equal legal rights.
details.simpleTerms: ACT's approach is broadly pro-freedom, pro-business and focused on personal responsibility, with a preference for a smaller, more efficient government, lower regulatory burdens and stronger property and individual rights.
details.caveat: This describes ACT's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether ACT's claims about its record are correct. Claims made by ACT about savings, crime, economic performance or the effects of its policies should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: Green Party
slogan: Campaigns on climate action and social and environmental policy.

details.overview: The Green Party is a left-wing political party that emphasises environmental protection, climate action, social and economic equality, strong public services, workers' rights and the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Its political philosophy combines environmentalism with social justice and a greater role for government in addressing inequality and providing essential services.
details.currentStatus: The party's current campaign slogan is "For All of Us."

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support a more progressive tax system in which higher-income and high-wealth individuals contribute more, with additional government investment directed towards public services, housing, infrastructure and reducing poverty.

policyAreas.title: Climate & environment
policyAreas.text: Make rapid reductions in greenhouse-gas emissions, phase down fossil-fuel use, expand renewable energy and protect native ecosystems, waterways and biodiversity. The Greens are proposing a national electrification plan covering homes, transport and industry.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase public investment in healthcare and improve access to timely, affordable services, including greater support for mental-health services and the health workforce.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Treat access to a warm, safe and affordable home as a basic need. Policies focus on increasing public and affordable housing, improving housing quality and addressing housing costs.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Support higher incomes, stronger employment protections, collective bargaining and policies intended to improve workers' living standards.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support well-funded public education from early childhood through tertiary education, with an emphasis on accessibility, inclusion and reducing financial barriers to study.

policyAreas.title: Cost of living
policyAreas.text: Reduce household costs through measures involving housing, public transport, electricity and essential services. The Greens' current priorities specifically include making housing, transport, groceries and power bills more affordable.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & land use
policyAreas.text: Promote more sustainable farming and forestry practices, protect waterways and soils, and support a food and fibre sector that reduces environmental impacts while maintaining rural employment.

policyAreas.title: Law & justice
policyAreas.text: Focus more strongly on preventing crime and addressing its underlying causes, alongside rehabilitation and reform of the justice system. The Greens generally favour a less punitive approach than National or ACT.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Te Tiriti
policyAreas.text: Support a stronger role for Te Tiriti o Waitangi in government and public decision-making, including greater recognition of Māori self-determination and the rights of iwi and hapū.

policyAreas.title: Drug policy
policyAreas.text: Support a health-based approach to drug use and drug-law reform, placing greater emphasis on harm reduction and treatment rather than criminal punishment.

policyAreas.title: Foreign affairs & defence
policyAreas.text: Promote an independent New Zealand foreign policy, international cooperation, human rights, peace and climate action, with opposition to greater military alignment where the Greens believe it compromises New Zealand's independence.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Place strong emphasis on reducing poverty and inequality and improving outcomes for children, disabled people, women, rainbow communities and other groups experiencing disadvantage.

policyAreas.title: Business & industry
policyAreas.text: Support small and local businesses and sustainable industries, while favouring stronger regulation of large corporations where the Greens believe corporate power or environmental impacts are harming the public interest.

details.position: The Greens are generally positioned on the left, with a combination of environmentalism, social democracy, progressive social policy and stronger government intervention in the economy. Compared with Labour, the Greens generally advocate more aggressive climate action, greater redistribution of wealth, stronger environmental regulation and a larger expansion of public services.
details.simpleTerms: The Greens' approach is broadly pro-environment, pro-public services and focused on reducing inequality, with government playing a significant role in redistributing wealth, providing essential services, addressing climate change and protecting the environment.
details.caveat: This describes the Green Party's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether previous Green policies have succeeded. Claims made by the Greens about the economy, climate, poverty or government performance should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: Labour Party
slogan: Campaigns on jobs, health and housing from a centre-left platform.

details.overview: Labour is a centre-left political party that emphasises strong public services, workers' rights, affordable housing, reducing inequality and government investment in health, education and infrastructure. Its current policy priorities are broadly centred on jobs, health and homes.
details.currentStatus: Labour is currently in Opposition, led by Chris Hipkins.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support an economy focused on good jobs, decent wages, investment and productivity. Labour also proposes using government investment to support New Zealand businesses and infrastructure.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase access to publicly funded healthcare. Current policies include three free GP visits per year for everyone, removing the $5 prescription charge, and expanding access to other health services.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support accessible public education, improve educational outcomes and invest in schools, teachers and student support.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Increase the supply of affordable homes, support home ownership and strengthen public and affordable housing provision.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Emphasise employment standards, fair pay, job security and workers' rights, while supporting apprenticeships and skills development.

policyAreas.title: Infrastructure & transport
policyAreas.text: Increase investment in infrastructure and make public transport more affordable. Labour's current policy includes a $20 weekly public-transport fare cap in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and $10 elsewhere.

policyAreas.title: Business & industry
policyAreas.text: Establish a New Zealand Future Fund to invest in infrastructure and innovative New Zealand businesses, alongside policies aimed at supporting domestic industry and investment.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Support greater investment in renewable energy and emissions reduction. Labour's current SolarSaver policy would provide government-backed finance to reduce the upfront cost of installing solar power.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Focus on reducing poverty and inequality and providing support for families, children and people experiencing hardship.

policyAreas.title: Treaty & Māori policy
policyAreas.text: Labour supports the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and opposes policies it considers to weaken Māori rights or the Treaty relationship.

details.position: Labour is generally positioned on the centre-left, favouring a larger role for government in providing public services, supporting workers and addressing inequality. It generally places greater emphasis than National on government investment, social programmes, employment protections and universal access to public services.
details.simpleTerms: Labour's approach is broadly pro-public services, pro-worker and focused on reducing inequality, with government playing a significant role in healthcare, education, housing, infrastructure and economic development.
details.caveat: This describes Labour's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies have succeeded. Claims made by Labour about the economy, government performance or the effects of its policies should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: National Party
slogan: Campaigns on economic management from a centre-right platform.

details.overview: National is a centre-right political party that emphasises economic growth, lower taxes, individual responsibility, private enterprise, public-service performance and law and order. Its stated values include ambition, success, rewarding hard work and equal opportunity.
details.currentStatus: National currently leads the New Zealand Government under Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. Its current political programme is centred on "fixing the basics and building the future."

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Promote economic growth, productivity, investment and exports; maintain relatively low taxes; reduce government spending and debt.

policyAreas.title: Infrastructure
policyAreas.text: Increase investment in roads, housing-enabling infrastructure, schools, hospitals and other major projects, alongside resource-management reform intended to make development easier.

policyAreas.title: Law & order
policyAreas.text: Tougher penalties for serious offending, stronger action against gangs, additional police powers and greater police visibility.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase access to healthcare, reduce waiting times, expand medicines and surgical capacity, and improve primary and after-hours care.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Greater emphasis on reading, writing and mathematics, classroom resources and measurable educational achievement. National is also replacing NCEA with a new national qualification framework.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Increase housing supply through planning and resource-management reform, infrastructure investment and changes intended to make development easier.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & business
policyAreas.text: Support the primary sector, exports, investment and business growth, with an emphasis on reducing regulatory barriers.

policyAreas.title: Foreign affairs & defence
policyAreas.text: Strengthen New Zealand's defence capability and international partnerships, particularly interoperability with Australia. National has stated that it intends to increase defence spending substantially if re-elected.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Supports emissions reduction while placing greater emphasis on economic impacts, technological solutions and maintaining productive industries.

details.position: National is generally positioned on the centre-right, economically favouring lower taxation, private enterprise and restrained government spending, while supporting government provision of core services such as health, education, infrastructure and policing.
details.simpleTerms: National's approach is broadly pro-business, pro-growth and fiscally conservative, combined with a strong emphasis on public-service performance, infrastructure development, education standards and tougher law-and-order policies.
details.caveat: This describes National's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies have succeeded. Where National makes claims about its record (such as reductions in crime or improvements in the economy), those should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.
